text:
Berkly Catton's eight-game point streak ended in Finland, where Carolina beat Seattle twice, but the 20-year-old's second season still looks like a different player from his first. The eighth pick in 2024 has 14 points in 18 games after 0.26 a game as a rookie, with his ice time up to 15:09 from 12:56 and a bigger share of the power play.

The good news first. Seattle gets 53% of the 5v5 expected goals (chance quality) with him on the ice, almost 13 points better than without him, and forwards picked sixth to tenth since 2005 scored a median 0.41 points a game in their first full season. He's at 0.78.

The warning label: his last ten games produced ten points against the 5.3 we'd expect, while his own chances in that stretch (0.9 expected goals) were half his usual. Our numbers call that mostly bounces. He's shooting 20% against a talent range near 13%. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had more than half his shots coming off the rush. The role is real. The scoring pace will probably cool before it settles.
headline: Catton's breakout, with a warning label
